brief.subject: Fake passport help and debt relief impersonators hit by FTC
brief.headline: FTC targets passport-service impersonators as court shuts down debt relief scheme
brief.dek: Two FTC actions take aim at operations that posed as government agencies or banks, plus a new report on fraud against older adults.
brief.lede: Scammers posing as government agencies are in regulators' sights this week. The FTC sued an alleged passport-services impersonator and won a permanent ban against a debt relief scheme that targeted seniors.

sections.heading: Passport help that isn't the government
bullets: The FTC sued GovAssist LLC, Entry LLC and Scott Zuckerman over an alleged government impersonation scheme.
People seeking passport services were allegedly misled into thinking the operation was, or was tied to, the federal government.
The FTC says paid search ads were used to pose as the government, so top search results aren't proof a site is official.
The complaint also cites misleading promises and fake reviews, meaning glowing ratings shouldn't settle whether a service is legitimate.

sections.heading: Debt relief scheme permanently banned
bullets: A federal court permanently banned operators of an alleged debt relief scheme, acting at the FTC's request.
The scheme allegedly targeted seniors and veterans by posing as banks, credit card companies and government agencies.
On October 14, 2026, the court entered a $106.8 million default judgment against corporate defendants.
Unsolicited debt relief pitches claiming to come from a bank or agency deserve extra scrutiny, especially for older relatives.

sections.heading: New FTC report on older adults
bullets: The FTC sent Congress its Protecting Older Consumers 2025-2026 report on fraud affecting older Americans.
It draws on fraud reports filed by older adults to flag key trends in how they are targeted.
The report also details FTC enforcement against deceptive practices aimed at older consumers, useful context for families helping parents.

brief.seo_description: FTC sues alleged passport-service impersonators, a court bans a debt relief scheme targeting seniors, and a new report on fraud against older adults.
